steps.caption: Pipeline
steps.narration: Give a job a budget, and the CRM compares it with what you spend.

steps.caption: Open the job
steps.narration: Open the job from the Pipeline. Here, the Wrenhaven reception flooring job, in White Plains.

steps.caption: Budget is zero
steps.narration: Its Budget box is still at zero.

steps.caption: The entry row
steps.narration: Budgets are set on the Costing tab, with this entry row.

steps.caption: Cost code
steps.narration: Pick a cost code. Cost codes sort a job's money by type of work, like Flooring.

steps.caption: Notes
steps.narration: Add a note if you like.

steps.caption: Amount
steps.narration: Type the budget for that code.

steps.caption: The Flooring line
steps.narration: Flooring now has a line, with its budget.

steps.caption: A second code
steps.narration: Add a line for every code you want to track. Next, Finish Carpentry.

steps.caption: A line per code
steps.narration: Each code has its own line: budget, committed, actual and variance.

steps.caption: Variance
steps.narration: Variance is the budget minus the actual cost. Nothing is spent yet, so it equals the budget.

steps.caption: The total budget
steps.narration: At the top, the Budget box adds your lines together.

steps.caption: Where to find it
steps.narration: Open any job from Pipeline, in the left menu.

youtube.title: How to set a budget for a job | ConstructHUB CRM
youtube.description: Set a job's budget by cost code in the ConstructHUB CRM. Open the job, add a budget line for each cost code on the Costing tab, and read the Budget total and the Variance column. Recorded in a demo workspace with a made-up client.
